applies_why: The judge text issues an UNDERDETERMINED verdict for an Acts 2:30 row by treating competing readings as unresolved, which is what K-S2 governs.
quote: D5 vs C1 (Acts 2:30): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] and [CR3] answered the loins/seed row with Genesis 46:26 and Hebrews 7:10 (loins at depth) and the legal/flesh distinction, while [DR3] presses that the only named Davidic man is Joseph; neither chain forces the other.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand — I weighed whether this forbids UNDERDETERMINED when the row verse is read two ways, or only requires both readings to be counted.
why: The judge declares Acts 2:30 UNDERDETERMINED by leaving the loins/seed row unresolved between loins-at-depth and the named-man reading, which K-S2 forbids because a two-sense verse is not open.
